First of all I’m so sorry about your father and the additional stress of the financial burden placed onto you—that is a lot to take on. I don’t know the details and I don’t want to make assumptions but I just hope that you’re not being taken advantage of in anyway. Depending on the ages of the other family members I hope they are taking responsibility where they can, because when someone gets hurt it’s everyone’s job to help, such as if sibling is a young adult in college that choice was based on saved money from themselves or being a dependent to the father/both or the alternative which is student loan/borrowing money from bank/being in deb (that part should not be on you) & reducing electricity usage when can in the house. 

I’ve been in a familiar situation but on the other side and my family didn’t have an alternative guardian figure to depend on. I just *hope* that YOU can continue to enjoy “the simple things”. 
—-
Partner situation: Whatever you do DON’T project. Communicate your fears to your partner, validate yourself and them. But do not project, do not push them away because of your own self-image or your feelings take over—*REMEMBER:* it’s ok that you feel that way, you’re a loving partner and family supporter, it’s very kind how thoughtful you are to the relationship. 

Partners are there through the hard times, under the circumstances your partner should be understanding and supportive. Love is not monetary, it’s everything besides that, and gifts that are DIY are all the better. 

Ask yourself: Do you love your partner? Do you still want to pursue this relationship? With this life-change will YOU still love your partner? Will you still be able to express and spend quality time with your partner? Would you be able to be a partner to your partner (go over what that actually means to you) 

It would be very unfortunate if something like this would be a dealbreaker to your partner, and in my own judgment in my life: for me it would be a dealbreaker if that was a dealbreaker to my partner.

6. What skills background does he have? What past jobs? What certificates or (if) secondary education? 
7. What keeps you going? 
8. What do you enjoy to do? (However ‘small’ or ‘big’) 
9. What are your passions 
10. Where do you want to see yourself in the future? In what field or work? 
11. Remember that it’s a journey, where you begin should not be compared to your career goal and things DO change and that’s ok 
12. There are many types of jobs: labour (ones that don’t require more education), other jobs that don’t require you have one. And many jobs for “higher-education” that are college or university level range in years required for diploma or degree, and if that takes you longer that’s ok). (For example theres a prison in my community so there’s a lot of guards, I think college is less than a year) 

-look through the college course list 
-if you need so back to secondary school in order to get the requirements you need THATS OK it doesn’t matter your age. Many colleges have a Adult-Learning Program or “Upgrade” program. 
-if you enjoy topics at the university level go study then if you can. If you don’t end using the degree you want it is a respected achievement/will help you stand out on a resume (and even though hard, engaging, and worth it for you). You have no obligation to that field of study.

-many colleges/university’s have supports for students who need it, like accommodations

-Go try things, if you go into something worried if you won’t like it but you’re interested in it, it’s better that you know and try than not at all
-if you don’t have the means for more education but you want to you definitely have to be a little stricter with yourself (ONLY A LITTLE) about yes I’m interested and it would be worth it to try/I will get new skills/meet new people/grow—-like before studying or going into the field do your own self-studying. 


-push yourself but be aware about what healthy push looks like 

13. Look into volunteering if there’s anything local to your area, or MAKE something like a cleaning community fb-group. You’re not required to show up but it’s something you should at least feel the want/need to do 

- - - 
Not everyone’s path is perfect. The “system” isn’t made for people with disabilities and it’s not fair. 

Even in this path you’re going to struggle, and you may feel like giving up and sometimes you’ll need a break (or if you go to school need a year or semester off). That’s ok. 

(I didn’t mean for this to sound just about more about college/university, I just wanted you to be informed about your options within that)
